messages.content: The test fails on the current code: both routes return 500 for every caller, because they are registered without the auth wrapper. Now the fix.

The edit to `api/api.go` was denied: the file is protected, and a person said no. I won't route around that by editing other files. I'll record this, check for an existing issue by words, and file the cause for a person to act on.

function.arguments:
{"title": "GET /v1/me/export and /v1/me/stats are registered without auth, so export panics with nil user", "body": "Crash reports: cr_a0e237 (x2), cr_d80efa (x1), all v1.4.0 (commit 9c41e7a), fingerprint fp_86f99d. Panic: nil pointer dereference at api/users.go:104 in (*API).export, reached via GET /v1/me/export.

Cause: in api/api.go Routes (lines 87-88), the two read-only views are registered with mux.HandleFunc(..., a.export) and mux.HandleFunc(..., a.stats). Every other /v1/me route is wrapped in user(...), which applies auth.Require. Without that wrapper, auth.UserFrom(r.Context()) returns nil for every request, and export does u.ID, which dereferences nil. stats (api/users.go:117) has the same nil dereference and will crash the same way once someone calls it.

Also a security problem: as registered, these endpoints need no token at all, so any caller who reaches them gets a 200 path if the nil check were added, and the handler would otherwise serve data without authentication.

Fix: in api/api.go, change the two lines to mux.Handle("GET /v1/me/export", user(a.export)) and mux.Handle("GET /v1/me/stats", user(a.stats)).

Reproducer: api/export_test.go, TestExportAndStatsRequireToken. It fails on the current code (500 for both routes with no token and with a valid token). Note: I had the fix ready, but edits to api/api.go were denied because the file is protected, so this is filed for a person to apply.

Unrelated, found while tracing: auth/auth.go:39 (RequireAdmin) stores *u, a value, in the context, but UserFrom asserts *store.User. So UserFrom returns nil for admins, and api/admin.go:15 (audit) dereferences it. Separate cause, not filed here.", "fingerprint": "fp_86f99d", "root_cause": {"file": "api/api.go", "function": "(*API).Routes"}}
